title: Japan's Hotels Struggle to Find Enough Workers
paragraphs: More and more foreign tourists are visiting Japan. But many hotels and traditional Japanese inns, called ryokan, do not have enough workers.

According to the Japan Tourism Agency's 2026 white paper on tourism, which was released in July 2026, more than 70% of places to stay in Japan do not have enough staff. The agency did a survey from December to January, and 522 hotels, ryokan and other places to stay answered. Of these, 72.2% said they did not have enough workers.

Why is it hard to find workers? According to the white paper, one reason is that wages are relatively low. Another reason is that workers often get few days off. These problems make it difficult for hotels to hire new staff.

The Tourism Agency says that hotels need to pay their workers more and improve their working conditions. The white paper also shared some examples of hotels that found new ideas. For example, some hotels close on days when they usually have few guests. Other hotels share workers. When one hotel is busy and another is quiet, workers from the quiet hotel go to help at the busy hotel.

The problem is not only in hotels. According to the research company Teikoku Databank, about half of all Japanese companies did not have enough full-time workers in April 2026. The company also found that 441 companies went bankrupt in the 2025 business year because they could not find enough workers. This was 26% more than the year before.
In an earlier survey by Teikoku Databank in January 2025, more than half of hotel and ryokan businesses said they did not have enough workers.
